[00:00] Maya: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We just wanted to run through the kickoff, make sure we capture scope for a three week pilot and get the network/security folks aligned.
[00:10] Lena: Yeah hi all, thanks. Just so you know we have a hard requirement for private connectivity and keys managed in house, that's non-negotiable because of our regulatory gating.
[00:18] Ethan: Totally understood. We prefer to run the pilot in Redwood Private (VPC) for that exact reason, we'll need to verify VPC peering, security groups, and KMS integration. Quick question — do you have a preferred KMS provider?
[00:30] Oliver: We're using AWS KMS with an internal key policy tied to our audit account, um and we also rotate keys via an internal process. We'll need to validate that Redwood's key wrap and ephemeral access model fits into our KMS lifecycle.
[00:46] Maya: Perfect, that's helpful. We'll send a short KMS checklist and our recommended key lifecycle for Private installs.
[00:53] Samir: On the ML side — our main worry is latency. Our product uses short prompt completions frequently (200-400 tokens) and we need p95 to be under 150ms in production to keep the UI feeling snappy. Cost is important but latency comes first for this flow.
[01:10] Ethan: Great, that's the kind of detail we need. Two quick follow-ups: what's your expected QPS for those short flows during peak, and do you do session caching or KV caching on your side?
[01:22] Samir: Peak is about 18 QPS for the web flow, but we could burst to 35 on flash events. We don't have a caching layer yet — we've been relying on the model context. We're open to Redwood's prefix/KV cache recommendations.
[01:34] Jenna: Also to add, our product has a few longer generation use-cases, like 1–2k tokens for weekly digest generation, those are batch jobs and can be scheduled. So we want both low-latency online and throughput for batch.
[01:48] Rina: That's an ideal pilot scope — shows both interactive and batch characteristics. For Dedicated sizing we'll model for 20 QPS sustained with 40 QPS burst capability and separate batch workers.
[02:00] Lena: Budget wise — we want to validate that Redwood gives us lower unit-cost than building in-house. We have internal infra costs but are concerned about ops overhead. The pilot will help decide.
[02:12] Maya: Understood. We'll provide a pricing comparison spreadsheet versus typical cluster costs. We'll also show quantization and batching options to get cost down without hurting quality.
[02:23] Oliver: Security question — do you have SOC2 attestation and can you provide the report and an architecture diagram for the Private bundle? Also, audit logs retention — we need 1 year of immutable logs for certain flows.
[02:38] Ola: Yes, Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we'll share the RCP and our standard architecture diagram, plus how audit logs are boxed in Private deployments. Audit log retention for the pilot can be configured; we'll note the retention policy and where logs are stored.
[02:52] Samir: When you say Private, is that fully air-gapped on-prem or VPC-hosted with customer peering? We have an eventual desire for on-prem for certain customers, but for pilot VPC peering is fine.
[03:05] Ethan: For pilot we recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your infra. Full on-prem is a separate package but we can discuss requirements later. VPC peering keeps latency low and still allows Redwood to manage the runtime.
[03:17] Jenna: Can you walk through the instrumentation and what we get in the Console for token-level cost and latency traces?
[03:24] Ola: Absolutely — the Console gives per-route breakdowns, token counts, model variant latencies, and traces tied to request IDs. We can show a demo of the telemetry but for now we'll include screenshots and sample export.
[03:36] Maya: One logistic — we'd like Samir's team to share representative prompt sets and a 14-day token histogram so we can size the Dedicated pool and estimate cost. That will feed into the Dedicated sizing spreadsheet.
[03:49] Samir: I can get that. It's probably a CSV with request timestamps and token counts, we sanitize PII before we send.
[03:56] Oliver: On data residency — some of our customers require EU-only processing, but our main product is US first. For the pilot we want US regions only, but we need to confirm Redwood can pin regions if we go multi-region later.
[04:12] Ethan: Yes, region pinning is possible — we'll document the options. For dedicated pools we can reserve capacity per region.
[04:19] Lena: On success criteria — for us the pilot should demonstrate: latency p95 <= 150ms for 200–400 token flows, steady-state cost per 1k tokens below our threshold (we'll provide), and successful KMS integration with logs flowing to our SIEM.
[04:34] Maya: Good measurable criteria. We'll align the pilot runbook to those.
[04:38] [brief cross-talk / laughter as someone drops audio]
[04:45] Ethan: A couple of technical notes I want to flag: model variants — you can start with an open Llama-style medium-sized model and we can try quantized variants to save CPU/GPU memory. We'll include benchmarks for expected latency at your sequence lengths. Also, prefix/KV caching can reduce per token compute for sessioned users.
[05:05] Samir: When you say quantized, are you referring to 8-bit or 4-bit? We've seen quality regressions with aggressive quantization.
[05:14] Ethan: Good point. We'll propose 8-bit quant profiles first; our Optimize team also runs quality regressions against your prompt set to ensure there's no meaningful drop. We'll include that in the pilot scope.
[05:26] Jenna: Who's the main technical contact from Redwood for the pilot?
[05:30] Maya: Ethan will be the SE lead for the pilot, Ola will handle Console/setup, and Rina will run the Customer Success coordination. I'm the account lead.
[05:39] Maya: We'll also schedule a dry-run for the infra handoff — VPC peering and KMS tests — ideally the week after next.
[05:46] Lena: That works.
[05:48] Oliver: One more security detail — our legal team needs to validate data retention and deletion flows. Can you describe how Redwood handles stored artifacts and the purge process?
[05:58] Ola: For Private installations, customer data isn't persisted beyond the configured retention window unless you intentionally enable logging of content. We can provide a retention matrix, and for the pilot we can set short retention and then extend if needed.
[06:10] Samir: We also want to run a small synthetic benchmark — can Redwood run a throughput/latency harness against a staging endpoint?
[06:18] Ethan: Yes, we'll provision a staging endpoint in your VPC peered environment and provide a script you can run. We'll also run our own synthetic suite and share the raw results.
[06:27] Jenna: Timeline question — how long does it usually take to spin up a pilot like this?
[06:31] Rina: Typically 7–10 business days to get networking and security signoffs and a staging environment, then a three week pilot window. So roughly a month end-to-end if there are no blockers.
[06:44] Lena: That seems reasonable. Our internal timeline is to decide by mid-August, so that aligns.
[06:50] Maya: Great. We'll recap next steps and owners.
[06:53] [silence / someone typing]

Sunward will share token telemetry, representative prompts (sanitized), and KMS/provider contacts. We'll schedule the VPC/KMS dry-run week of 7/26 and a security deep-dive with Oliver on 7/27. Does that reflect everyone's understanding?
[07:16] Lena: Yes.
[07:18] Samir: Yep.
[07:19] Oliver: Yep, please make sure the SOC2 excerpts include details about key management and logging.
[07:25] Maya: Will do. Anything else?
[07:28] Jenna: Can you also include a short demo deck of the Console—like 10 slides—so product stakeholders can quickly see observability?
[07:35] Ola: We'll attach a one-page Console primer and a 10-slide deck.
[07:40] Maya: Thank you all. We'll follow up with the docs and scheduling invites.
[07:44] Ethan: We'll also include initial latency sims for the 200–400 token flows and a note on expected p95 under the proposed Dedicated sizing.
[07:54] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[07:56] Maya: Thanks, meeting adjourned.
